_about: Hand-kept viewpoints for the discovery places layer (engine/discover/build.py via discover.json). Each is a place the City of Toronto's own open data describes as having a view (source: which dataset and entry), at the City's point for it. 'why' is our own words; 'checked' is the day the view and the place were last confirmed against the source (scouting/discovery/stale.py lists any over 180 days old). same_as: names of the City's rows for the same place, which this entry replaces (their link is kept). Candidates seen only in OpenStreetMap (Sauriol Cliff, the Vista Trail Viewing Platform, Lake Lookout in Downsview Park) are left out until a second source confirms them.
credit: Layers.City, from the City of Toronto's descriptions

places.name: Riverdale Park East
places.why: A park on the slope of the Don Valley, known for its wide view of the downtown skyline.
places.source: StrollTO: Riverdale Park East; Cultural Hotspot: Riverdale Park

places.name: Chester Hill Lookout
places.why: A small, hidden lookout where the downtown skyline rises over the trees of the Don Valley.
places.source: StrollTO and Cultural Hotspot: Chester Hill Lookout

places.name: Sheldon Lookout
places.why: At the northeast end of Humber Bay Shores Park, looking across the water to the downtown skyline.

places.name: Humber Bay Park East
places.why: Its eastern shore faces straight back at downtown across the bay: one of the classic skyline photos.
places.source: StrollTO and Cultural Hotspot: Humber Bay Park East

places.name: Governor's Lookout, Don Valley Brick Works Park
places.why: A lookout inside the park, with views over the surrounding valley.
places.source: StrollTO: Don Valley Brick Works Park

places.name: Baldwin Steps
places.why: A long public staircase with landings and a view of the skyline. It's in Scott Pilgrim.

places.name: Hillcrest Park
places.why: A park on the Davenport hill with a view over the city to Lake Ontario.

places.name: Sir Winston Churchill Park
places.why: A park with tennis courts, a playground and a view out over the city.

places.name: Sorauren Avenue Park
places.why: A neighbourhood park in Roncesvalles with a view east to the downtown skyline.

places.name: Wallace Avenue Footbridge
places.why: A footbridge over the rail corridor with views of the neighbourhood and the downtown skyline.
places.source: StrollTO: Wallace Avenue Footbridge & 371 Wallace Avenue

places.name: Eglinton Hill
places.why: A steep street where, on the way down, a wide view opens up to the west.

places.name: Centre Island Pier
places.why: A pier on Centre Island, with views across the lake one way and back to the skyline the other.

places.name: James Gardens
places.why: Gardens in the Humber Valley with a lookout over the valley to downtown.

places.name: CN Tower View Point, Colonel Samuel Smith Park
places.why: A spot on the Etobicoke waterfront looking east along the lake to the skyline and the CN Tower.
places.source: Cultural Hotspot: CN Tower View Point

places.name: Ski hill, Earl Bales Park
places.why: From the top of the ski hill you can see the skylines of both downtown and Yonge Street north of York Mills.
